quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter b: a tall stem with a round bump on its right, sitting on the baseline.
quests.question: b
quests.hint: Pull down from the top line. Go back up the stem to the middle line, then circle around to the right and close at the stem.
quests.explanation: b is a tall stem plus a small circle. It is the opposite of d, whose circle is on the left. Remember that b has its belly to the right, like a bump.
quests.funFact: The sound of b is made by pressing both lips together and letting a little air burst out.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter p: a stem that goes below the baseline, with a round bump at the top right.
quests.question: p
quests.hint: Start at the middle line, pull the stem all the way below the baseline, go back up a little and circle to the right.
quests.explanation: p has a descender and a circle on its right. The circle sits between the middle line and the baseline, like a small o attached to the stem.
quests.funFact: The letter p is the first letter of the word 'pencil', 'paper' and 'pen'.

quests.instruction: Write b and p side by side. One stem goes up, one goes down.
quests.question: b p
quests.hint: b's stem rises to the top line. p's stem drops under the baseline. Both circles face right.
quests.explanation: Same bump, opposite stems. When the bump sits on the right, you know the letter is b or p, not d or q.
quests.funFact: The letters b and p are both made by closing the lips, so linguists call their sounds bilabial.

quests.instruction: From memory, write h, n and m in a row. Count the arches in each.
quests.question: h n m
quests.hint: h has one arch and a tall stem, n has one arch, m has two. Check the arches are the same size.
quests.explanation: Counting arches is a quick check on your own work. It also helps you remember which letter is which.
quests.funFact: In ancient Rome, builders used arches to make strong bridges and aqueducts.

quests.instruction: Write b, h and p. Each has a stem and a bump or arch.
quests.question: b h p
quests.hint: b goes up and has a circle, h goes up and has an arch, p goes down and has a circle. Check heights.
quests.explanation: Looking for stems and the shapes attached to them is how you rebuild these letters from memory.
quests.funFact: In printing, the long vertical part of a letter such as b or h is called the stem.

quests.instruction: Write r, n, m, h in order, going from smallest to largest.
quests.question: r n m h
quests.hint: r is a half arch, n is one arch, m is two arches, h has a tall stem. Space them evenly.
quests.explanation: Ordering from simple to complex helps you see how the arch can be repeated or built upon.
quests.funFact: The ancient Greeks were among the first to write vowels as separate letters.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter e: a short line to the right, then a curve around and open at the bottom.
quests.question: e
quests.hint: Start at the middle of the letter and draw a line to the right. Then curve up, left, down and around, stopping at the bottom right.
quests.explanation: e starts with a horizontal stroke and then curves like c. The bar in the middle makes it different from c.
quests.funFact: The letter e appears in more English words than any other letter.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter s: a small version of the capital S, between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.question: s
quests.hint: Start at the top right and curve left, then swing through the middle and curve down and around to the bottom left.
quests.explanation: Lowercase s is a double curve. Going slowly in the middle keeps the two curves balanced.
quests.funFact: A long hissing sound, like a snake's, is often written as a string of s's.

quests.instruction: Write e and s together. Both are small and curvy.
quests.question: e s
quests.hint: Both letters fit between the middle line and the baseline. e is closed in the middle, s is a smooth double curve.
quests.explanation: Small curvy letters can easily wobble, so check the size and keep them exactly the same height.
quests.funFact: The letter s is found at the end of a lot of English words, since it makes plurals.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter f: a tall curved stem with a bar across the middle.
quests.question: f
quests.hint: Start at the top right, curve left and down the stem to the baseline. Then cross it with a short bar at the middle line.
quests.explanation: f has a curve at the top, a straight stem and a crossbar. It is an ascender, so it reaches the top line.
quests.funFact: In old books, a letter called the long s looked like an f without a full crossbar.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter k: a tall stem with a small arrow-like shape pointing to it.
quests.question: k
quests.hint: Pull down from the top line. Then, from the middle line, slant in to touch the stem and slant back out to the baseline.
quests.explanation: k is a stem and two slants meeting at the stem. The slants should be in the lower half of the stem.
quests.funFact: The letter k is silent when it comes before n at the start of English words, like 'knee' and 'knot'.

quests.instruction: Write f and k side by side. Both have tall stems.
quests.question: f k
quests.hint: Make both tall ones reach the top line. f has a crossbar and a curved top, k has two slants.
quests.explanation: Ascender letters reach the top line, and writing them side by side shows whether your heights match.
quests.funFact: The letter k is silent at the start of words like 'knee' and 'knife'.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter v: a small version of V, between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.question: v
quests.hint: Slant down to the baseline in a sharp point, then go up to the middle line.
quests.explanation: v is a pointed shape and has no curves. Its height is the same as c and o.
quests.funFact: The V shape is also the sign for victory, as in the peace sign.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter w: two v's joined together, between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.question: w
quests.hint: Slant down, up, down, up. Make four slants of equal length and keep both points on the baseline.
quests.explanation: w is two valleys joined. The middle peak should reach the middle line, not the baseline.
quests.funFact: In Welsh, the letter w can be a vowel, as in the word 'cwm'.

quests.instruction: Write v and w next to each other, both between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.question: v w
quests.hint: Make v with a sharp point, then make w with two. Check that each point touches the baseline.
quests.explanation: Pointed shapes need accurate stops. If the points drift above the baseline, the letters will float.
quests.funFact: Some birds, like geese, fly in a V formation.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter x: two slants crossing between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.question: x
quests.hint: Make the same two crossing slants as capital X, but only as tall as the small letters: from the middle line to the baseline.
quests.explanation: x is a small cross and has exactly the same height as c and o, which is why x-height is called that.
quests.funFact: The word 'xylophone' begins with an x that sounds like z.

quests.instruction: Write the lowercase letter z: a line across, a slant down, and a line across the bottom.
quests.question: z
quests.hint: Draw across at the middle line, slant down to the left, then draw across the baseline.
quests.explanation: z is three strokes and zigzags. Sharp corners at the top and bottom keep it clean.
quests.funFact: The sentence 'Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs' uses every letter of the alphabet, including z.

quests.instruction: Write x and z together. Both have sharp strokes.
quests.question: x z
quests.hint: x has two crossing slants, z has two bars and a slant. Both fit between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.explanation: Slants meet bars in z, and slants cross in x. Seeing those differences helps your memory.
quests.funFact: Dictionaries have only a few pages of words that begin with x.

quests.instruction: From memory, write v, w, x in a row.
quests.question: v w x
quests.hint: These are all slants. v is a valley, w is two valleys, x is a cross. Keep them the same height.
quests.explanation: Slanted letters share the same movement. Practising them together builds your angle control.
quests.funFact: In old-style writing, scribes used a quill pen cut at an angle so strokes were thick or thin.

quests.instruction: Write k, z and y in a row. They all have slants.
quests.question: k z y
quests.hint: k is a tall stem with slants, z has a bar and slant combination, y has two slants and a tail.
quests.explanation: Three slanted letters, three different heights. Plan each height before you write.
quests.funFact: Runes, an old alphabet of northern Europe, are made mostly of straight lines because they were carved into wood and stone.

quests.instruction: Write w, x, y and z in alphabetical order.
quests.question: w x y z
quests.hint: Say the letters as you write. Check that w, x and z are on the baseline, and y drops below.
quests.explanation: The last four letters have lots of slants. Writing them in order in lowercase shows control of angles.
quests.funFact: Many scripts that are used in India, such as Malayalam, were once written by scratching letters onto palm leaves.

quests.instruction: Write the tall letters b, d and h in a row. Each should reach the top line.
quests.question: b d h
quests.hint: Make every stem start at the top line. Check that all three are the same height before you move on.
quests.explanation: Letters whose stems reach the top line are called ascenders. They should all be the same height.
quests.funFact: The word 'ascender' comes from a Latin word meaning 'to climb up'.

quests.instruction: Write k, l and f together. Make the ascenders the same height.
quests.question: k l f
quests.hint: Stems start at the top line. f has a curved top, but it still reaches the top line.
quests.explanation: Same height for all tall letters is very important, so the text looks even.
quests.funFact: The lowercase letters b, d, f, h, k and l all have ascenders.

quests.instruction: Write t, l and b in a row and notice that t is shorter than the other two.
quests.question: t l b
quests.hint: t stops a little below the top line, while l and b reach the top line. Compare them.
quests.explanation: Not every letter with a stem is the same height. t is shorter than l and b.
quests.funFact: Handwriting practice lines often have a dotted middle line to show how tall small letters should be.

quests.instruction: Write g, j and p in a row. Each drops below the baseline.
quests.question: g j p
quests.hint: Start each tall part on the line, then let the stem go below the baseline. Keep the tails about the same length.
quests.explanation: The part of a letter that hangs below the baseline is a descender. Tails should be the same length.
quests.funFact: Some fonts shorten their descenders so that lines of text can sit closer together.

quests.instruction: Write q and y next to each other. Each has a tail below the line.
quests.question: q y
quests.hint: q has a straight tail, y has a slanted one. Both go below the baseline by the same amount.
quests.explanation: Straight tails and slanted tails are both descenders. Keep them from touching the line below.
quests.funFact: The word 'jiggly' has four descenders: j, g, g and y.

quests.instruction: Write g, y, p, q and j in a row. Check the tails.
quests.question: g y p q j
quests.hint: Plan the space first. Tails should go down the same length and not crash into each other.
quests.explanation: Five descenders make a good test. All of them must be even and not touch.
quests.funFact: Only five lowercase letters in the English alphabet have descenders in most handwriting: g, j, p, q and y.

quests.instruction: Write the small round letters a, c and e in a row. All three should be the same height.
quests.question: a c e
quests.hint: Check the middle line and the baseline. Each letter should fit exactly between them.
quests.explanation: x-height means the height of small letters, like a, c, e and x. Matching it makes writing look tidy.
quests.funFact: Fonts with a large x-height are often easier to read at small sizes.

quests.instruction: Write m, n, r and u, small letters with stems and arches, between the lines.
quests.question: m n r u
quests.hint: Check the stems start at the middle line and end at the baseline. Keep spaces the same.
quests.explanation: Four small letters in a row show if your x-height is steady. Check them against the middle line.
quests.funFact: Dotted lines on handwriting paper show where letters should start and stop.

quests.instruction: Write o, s, v, w, x and z from memory. All sit between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.question: o s v w x z
quests.correctAnswer: o s v w x z
quests.hint: Six small letters in a row: keep every one the same height. Slow down if one starts to float.
quests.explanation: Writing a long row of small letters needs you to remember the height each time.
quests.funFact: Thirteen lowercase letters have no tall stem, no tail and no dot: a, c, e, m, n, o, r, s, u, v, w, x and z.
